metadata.title: The replication package — comprising three Python scripts that reproduce Tables 2 through 6 and the cross-validation calculation, three pre-generated output files, a requirements.txt dependency statement, and a README document
metadata.description:
No new empirical data were collected for this study. All quantitative inputs used in the scenario analysis (Tables 2–6) are derived from publicly available primary sources: the NERSA MYPD6 Reasons for Decision (January 2025); the NERSA ERTSA FY2025/26 Reasons for Decision (March 2025); the Statistics South Africa Consumer Price Index Statistical Release P0141 (December 2025); the Statistics South Africa Electricity Generated and Available for Distribution P4141 (January 2026); the South African Reserve
Bank Monetary Policy Review (June 2015); the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy Integrated Resource Plan 2025; and the International Energy Agency Global Gas Security Review 2024. Full bibliographic details for all sources are provided in the reference list.

The replication package—comprising three Python scripts (dataset_tables1_4.py, replication_script_tables1_4.py, and
cross_validation_alessandri.py, requiring Python 3.9 or later, standard library only, and verified against Python 3.13) that reproduce Tables 2 through 6 and the cross-comparison analysis, three pre-generated output files, a requirements.txt dependency statement, and a README document—is available as supplementary material submitted with this manuscript [51]. Reviewers wishing to verify the arithmetic in Tables 2 through 6 may inspect the pre-generated output files directly without executing code; the output files reproduce every intermediate calculation and final figure appearing in the tables.

metadata.title: Replication package for a study of calibrated positional uncertainty in gazetteer resolution
metadata.description:
Code, derived result tables and figures replicating all quantitative results in an article currently under review at the Journal of Geovisualization and Spatial Analysis.

The package contains the full analysis pipeline (20 Python modules), 18 result tables backing every number reported in the paper, the LLM extraction cache (so the cross-generation transfer experiment reproduces with no API calls), the derived ~32k-row GeoNames subset the resolver runs against, and the 10 figures as submitted.

The method attaches a positional-uncertainty radius to each gazetteer-resolved place name and calibrates its scale by split-conformal prediction, so that a nominal-90% radius contains the true location at least 90% of the time. Coverage, sharpness, probability-integral-transform reliability, per-stratum (Mondrian) calibration, resolver-agnosticism, spatial autocorrelation of the residuals, and decision utility are all evaluated on two human-annotated English gold corpora (GeoVirus, GeoWebNews).

The two gold corpora are not redistributed here and must be obtained from their original authors (Gritta et al. 2018, 2020); see README.md for the full reproduction procedure.

This deposit is anonymised in its file contents for double-anonymous peer review.

metadata.title: django-smells: A Static Analysis Tool for Detecting Code Smells in Django Projects
metadata.description:
An open-source, AST-based static analysis tool that detects five Django-specific code smells spanning the Model, View, and Template layers. It uses Python's built-in ast module for checks within Python code, and a lightweight regex-based tokenizer over HTML templates.

This is the replication package for:

Django-Specific Code Smells: Catalog, Prevalence, and Automated Detection
Leopoldo Teixeira, Eduardo Luiz Silva
14th Workshop on Software Visualization, Evolution and Maintenance (VEM 2026), co-located with CBSoft 2026 — Short Paper track

Included in this archive:

  • The tool source code (zero runtime dependencies)
  • Its test suite
  • The RQ2 evaluation pipeline and results (a sample of 33 public Django repositories, 4,157 flagged occurrences)
  • The RQ3 manual-validation pipeline and results (50 manually reviewed occurrences, 88% overall precision)

Released under the MIT license. See the GitHub repository for full documentation, including instructions to reproduce each of the paper's research questions.

metadata.title: Replication package: Geometry-Aware Prompt Context for Model Consistency Management
metadata.description:
Replication package for the paper Geometry-Aware Prompt Context for Model Consistency Management.

Keeping independently developed models consistent with the help of a large language model requires prompting it about two metamodels at once, and industrial metamodels are too large to paste in wholesale. This package implements Anchored Geometric Propagation (AGP), which computes prompt context from metamodel structure: a small set of confirmed correspondences joins the two metamodels, candidates are ranked by geodesic distance over the joined pair blended with name similarity at a weight calibrated on those correspondences, confident matches are promoted to further anchors, and uncertain ones are deferred to an engineer.

Contents: the implementation and experiment runners, the metamodel pairs used as worked examples, all measurements as CSV files, the figures reported in the paper, and the prompts produced by each selection strategy.

metadata.title: Replication Package for: "Do Voters Punish Inflation or Pay Cuts? Inflation and Real Wages in U.S. Elections"
metadata.description:
# Replication package — *Do Voters Punish Inflation or Pay Cuts? Inflation and Real Wages in U.S. Elections*

Riaño and Trebbi, *Journal of Monetary Economics*.

This package reproduces **every table and figure in the paper and its online
appendix** from public raw data, end to end, with a single command. It is
self-contained: all code, data, and the vendored R library live inside this
folder, and no script reads anything outside it or reaches the network.

---

## 1. Software requirements

The results were produced with the following toolchain (macOS):

| Tool | Version used | Notes |
|------|--------------|-------|
| Stata SE | **StataNow 19.5** | regressions, data builds, labeling. Bootstrap SEs use `seed(1)`; exact bootstrap draws are reproducible on this Stata version. |
| R | **4.5.2** | data merges, maps, aggregation. **Use the vendored library in `code/r-lib/`** (see below); key packages: `sf` 1.0.24, `dplyr` 1.1.4, `readxl` 1.4.5, `readr` 2.1.6, `tidyr` 1.3.2, `haven` 2.5.5, `ggplot2` 4.0.1, `stringr` 1.6.0. |
| Python | **3.9.13** | table parsing, significance summaries, the motivating figure. Packages: `pandas` 2.3.3, `numpy` 2.0.2, `matplotlib` 3.9.4. |

`run_all.sh` points R at `code/r-lib/` automatically (via `R_LIBS`), so no R
packages need to be installed. For Python, create a virtual environment **inside
this package** and install the pinned packages from `requirements.txt`:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
```

`run_all.sh` auto-detects `.venv/` in this directory; otherwise it falls back to
`python3` on your `PATH`. You can always point it at a specific interpreter with
`PYTHON=/path/to/python`. Only a `.venv` *inside* this package is auto-detected —
a `.venv` elsewhere on your system is never picked up implicitly. `run_all.sh`
checks up front that the chosen interpreter can import the required packages and
stops with a clear message if not.

---

## 2. How to run

From **this directory**:

```bash
bash run_all.sh
```

Override any tool location via environment variables, e.g.:

```bash
STATA=/Applications/Stata/StataSE.app/Contents/MacOS/stata-se \
RSCRIPT=Rscript PYTHON=python3 \
bash run_all.sh
```

`run_all.sh` runs the whole pipeline in the correct order, creates all needed
`data/interim/` and `output/` subdirectories, and asserts that each step's key
output was produced before continuing (it stops with a clear error otherwise).
Per-step logs are written to `logs/`.

**Runtime:** **≈40 minutes** end to end, measured on the reference machine
(Stata SE 19.5, R 4.5.2, Python 3.9, macOS, SSD). The R county-data merges (`5a`–`5d`,
`5g`) and the Stata cluster-bootstrap specifications (`6h`/`6l`, 100 reps each) dominate;
allow more time on slower hardware or network-backed (e.g. cloud-synced) storage.

### How paths work
Scripts are anchored to this package root; they use only relative paths.
`run_all.sh` runs every step from the package root and exports `REPL_ROOT`
(for the R scripts' `setwd`) and `R_LIBS` (the vendored library). Stata scripts
capture the working directory with `` `c(pwd)' `` where needed. You do **not**
need to edit any path.

---

## 3. Folder structure

```
9-replication/
├── README.md ← this file
├── run_all.sh ← master script (run this)
├── output_crosswalk.csv ← every paper item → output file → script → inputs
├── code/ ← 49 analysis scripts (.do/.R/.py) + r-lib/ (vendored R packages)
├── data/
│ ├── raw/ ← public raw inputs (bundled; see §4)
│ │ └── gis/ ← shapefiles (county, congressional district, CPI PSU)
│ └── interim/ ← built .dta files (created by the pipeline)
├── output/
│ ├── figures/ ← all paper & appendix figures (.pdf)
│ ├── tables/ ← all paper & appendix tables (.tex)
│ └── <analysis subdirs>/ ← intermediate regression outputs (raw outreg2 .tex, CSVs)
└── logs/ ← per-step run logs (created by run_all.sh)
```

The manuscript's `\includegraphics{...}` / `\input{tables/...}` filenames match
the files produced in `output/figures/` and `output/tables/` exactly.

---

## 4. Data

All raw inputs required by the paper are **public** and are **bundled** in
`data/raw/` (≈0.46 GB), so the package runs out of the box. Raw inputs are kept
separate from the generated intermediates in `data/interim/`.

| Source (folder in `data/raw/`) | Origin | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `EPI_fbc/` | Economic Policy Institute, Family Budget Calculator (2022/2024/2025 releases) | local cost-of-living / inflation measures |
| `MITElectionLab/` | MIT Election Data and Science Lab (Harvard Dataverse): county presidential 2000–2024 & 1976–2020; House 1976–2024 | electoral outcomes |
| `tonmcg/` | `tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24` (GitHub) — 2024 county presidential results | Kansas 2024 rebuild + FIPS corrections |
| `uscensus/` | U.S. Census Bureau — 2020 Urban/Rural, county age/sex estimates, Decennial DP1 | demographic covariates |
| `usda/` | USDA ERS county indicators (Education, Poverty, Unemployment, Population) | covariates |
| `bea/` | Bureau of Economic Analysis — county ALL_AREAS (CAGDP1/2/9, CAINC1/4/30) | GDP / personal income covariates |
| `bls/` | BLS QCEW (annual county high-level, 2020/2021/2023/2024) and LAUS (`laus/`) | wages, employment, unemployment |
| `bls_cpi/`, `bls_cpi_annual/` | BLS CPI-U (PSU/category averages; All Items) | CPI benchmark, national time series |
| `bea_rpp/` | BEA Regional Price Parities (MARPP/MAIRPD/SARPP/SAIRPD) | EPI-vs-RPP validation |
| `crosswalk_cbsa_county/` | OMB CBSA delineation (July 2023) | county→metro crosswalk for RPP |
| `crosswalk_congressional_districts_counties/` | DailyKos/DOA county↔119th-CD crosswalk (`DOA_csv.zip`) | county→congressional-district aggregation |
| `zillow/` | Zillow ZHVI, county (`County_zhvi.csv`) | housing-price robustness control |
| `ReplicationPackage_Flavin2026/` | Flavin (2026, *Electoral Studies*) published replication data | Flavin replication + FHFA HPI / USDA-ERS robustness columns |
| `acs/` | Census ACS 5-year 2020, county median household income (DP03) | income-tercile heterogeneity (Figure 4a) |
| `gis/` | TIGER/Line 2024 county & congressional-district shapefiles; 2018 CPI PSU shapefile | maps and spatial joins |

**Not included** (confirmed **unused** by the paper's pipeline): Nielsen/Kilts
scanner data, `dcpi_data`, religion census, and a standalone FHFA folder (FHFA HPI
enters only through the Flavin replication file). These were part of the broader
research project but no paper table or figure depends on them.

If you need to refresh a source, re-download it from the origin above and place
it under `data/raw/` with the same subfolder and filenames.

---

## 5. Output locations and crosswalk

- **Figures:** `output/figures/*.pdf` **Tables:** `output/tables/*.tex`
- Intermediate regression outputs (raw `outreg2` `.tex`, coefficient CSVs) live in
the topical `output/*/` subdirectories and feed the final tables.

`output_crosswalk.csv` lists **all 99 paper/appendix items** with columns
*paper_item, output_file, output_path, generating_script(s), key_input_data*.
The main-paper items:

| Paper item | Output file | Generating script(s) |
|---|---|---|
| Figure 1 | `motivating_panel5_infl_bars_cum_lines.pdf` | `0-motivating_graphs.py` |
| Figure 2a | `cpi_psu_coverage.pdf` | `6n-cpi_coverage_map.R` |
| Figure 2b | `infl_21_24_total_2p2c.pdf` | `3-exploring_epi_fbc_data...R` |
| Figure 3 | `coefplot_dispersion.pdf` | `6z-category_dispersion.do` → `6z-...coefplot.R` |
| Figure 4a/4b | `coefplot_het_income.pdf` / `coefplot_het_urban.pdf` | `5o` → `6aa-heterogeneity_income.do` → `6aa-...coefplot.R` |
| Table 1 | `tab_sumstats.tex` | `6k-summary_statistics.do` → `6m-build_paper_tables.py` |
| Table 2 | `tab_baseline.tex` | `6h/6l` county `.do` → `6j-combine_se_tables.py` → `6m` |
| Table 3 | `tab_gap.tex` | `6h/6l` county `.do` → `6j` → `6m` |
| Table 4 | `tab_gaponly.tex` | `6h/6l` county `.do` → `6j` → `6m` |
| Table 5 | `tab_cd_heterogeneity.tex` | `6x-cd_heterogeneity.do` → `6mm-build_robustness_tables.py` |

Online-appendix items (maps `appendix_*`, EPI category maps `infl_21_24_*_2p2c`,
EPI-vs-RPP scatters `scatter_*`, binscatter/spline/heatmap panels, the
average-pay and congressional-district tables, robustness tables, the Flavin,
log-odds, and BEA-cascade tables, etc.) are enumerated in `output_crosswalk.csv`.

---

## 6. Pipeline stages (handled automatically by `run_all.sh`)

1. **Build datasets** — `1,2` (EPI county list & FBC) → `3` (long FBC + inflation maps)
→ `4a,4b` (presidential & House returns) → `5,5a–5d` (merge Census/USDA/BEA/QCEW)
→ `5e,5g,5i` (labels, county→CD) → `5j` (standardize, build wage–price gaps).
Auxiliary builds: `5k,5l` (BEA RPP), `5o` (ACS income), `5m` (robustness controls).
2. **Validation, robustness sources, figure analyses** — `6v` (EPI vs RPP), `6w`
(control sets), `6x` (CD heterogeneity), `6y` (national time series), `6z`
(dispersion), `6aa` (heterogeneity), `6bb,6cc` (pre-trends).
3. **Combined regressions → paper tables** — `6h`×4, `6l`×4 → `6j` (×2) →
`6k` → `6m` and `6mm`.
4. **Maps, benchmarks, nonlinearity, Flavin, log-odds** — `6n,6o,6p,6q,6s,6t`.
5. **Consolidate** the two figure families without an auto-copy step (the
motivating panel and the seven EPI inflation maps) into `output/figures/`.

Scripts can be rerun without deleting old outputs; each overwrites its own
targets, and `5j` is idempotent (guards the FBC dollars→thousands rescale).

---

## 7. Manual / ad-hoc data edits (documented, reproducible, in code)

Every non-general data adjustment is already implemented **in code** (no external
spreadsheet edits). They are centralized here for review; each remains in its
original script to preserve the exact numerical results. See also
`code/AD_HOC_EDITS.md`.

1. **BEA combined county-equivalents crosswalk** — `code/5c-build_county_data_3.R`
(`tribble`, ~lines 45–99). 26 BEA "combined-area" codes are mapped to their
component counties/cities (Maui+Kalawao `15901→15009`; 24 Virginia
independent-city groups, e.g. `51901→51003,51540`). The combined BEA figure is
**copied to each component** county. *Caveat:* for extensive quantities (GDP,
personal income) this attributes the whole combined-area total to each
component; it affects only BEA-based covariates in ~50 VA/HI counties. This is
a construction choice inherited from the source geography, documented here, and
left unchanged.
2. **2024 presidential FIPS corrections** — `code/4a-build_presidential_data_to_stata.R`
(~66–113). Scrambled MIT 2024 county FIPS in AZ, AR, CO, FL, GA are remapped
(2024 rows only).
3. **Kansas 2024 rebuild** — `4a` (~123–155). MIT's KS 2024 rows are dropped
("scrambled vote counts") and rebuilt from the `tonmcg` county returns.
4. **Texas OTHER-row drop** — `4a` (~177–195). For TX, only `TOTAL VOTES` rows are
kept; `OTHER` candidate rows are dropped to avoid inflated totals.
5. **Hand-entered national series** — `code/0-motivating_graphs.py` (~61–70). The
national CPI-U and average-hourly-earnings arrays for **Figure 1 only** are
typed inline (source: BLS). No other result uses them.
6. **Turnout caps / jurisdiction blanking** — `code/5j-standardize_final_datasets.do`.
Turnout capped at 100; turnout set missing for CT & RI (no county government);
two-party shares set missing where rep+dem votes are zero.
7. **Connecticut planning-region harmonization** — `code/1-build_listcounties_fips.do`
(~140–156). CT's nine 2022 planning regions are mapped onto historical counties
to match Census/BLS geography.
8. **Non-county aggregate drops** — `code/6bb`, `code/6cc` (`drop if county_fips>99999`)
remove non-county aggregate rows before the pre-trend regressions.

---

## 8. Randomness / seeds

The only randomness is Stata's cluster bootstrap for state-clustered standard
errors (`vce(bootstrap, cluster(statefe) reps(100) seed(1))`). **Every** bootstrap
sets `seed(1)`, so results are deterministic on a fixed Stata version. No R or
Python step uses sampling.

---

## 9. Known restrictions / notes

- **Stata SE 19.5** was used. Bootstrap standard errors reproduce exactly on the
same Stata version; other versions may differ in the last reported digits due to
RNG-stream differences (point estimates are unaffected).
- The package needs **no network access** and **no manual data download** — all
inputs are bundled in `data/raw/`.
- Figure 1's national series is hand-entered from BLS (item 7.5 above); it is the
only input without a raw data file.
- Everything else is fully automated by `run_all.sh`.
